title: Thermal oxide consumes the silicon underneath it
caption: Oxidant reaches the interface through the oxide, where reaction consumes silicon and grows the film. The interface is a boundary between materials, not a third material layer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Growing silicon dioxide
nodes.detail: Oxidant passes through the growing oxide to react at its lower boundary.

nodes.label: Remaining silicon
nodes.detail: Silicon is consumed at the moving silicon–oxide interface.

source.heading: 1. Thermal Oxidation: Growing SiO2 from the Wafer Itself

title: Choose the heating tool around the thermal budget
caption: Batch furnaces and rapid thermal tools expose wafers to different time-temperature histories. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Batch furnace
nodes.detail: Many wafers share a sustained thermal process.

nodes.label: Rapid thermal process
nodes.detail: A wafer heats and cools much more quickly.

nodes.label: Existing device structure
nodes.detail: Dopants and materials limit allowable thermal exposure.

title: A deposited atom arrives inside a molecule
caption: CVD couples gas transport, surface reaction and removal of volatile by-products. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Deliver precursor
nodes.detail: Gas flow transports source molecules toward the wafer.

nodes.label: Adsorb and react
nodes.detail: Surface chemistry releases the film-forming species.

nodes.label: Grow the solid film
nodes.detail: Deposited material accumulates on the substrate.

nodes.label: Remove by-products
nodes.detail: Volatile reaction products leave through the exhaust.

title: Different CVD families supply reaction energy differently
caption: Temperature, pressure and plasma assistance help match a film process to the device's thermal and geometric constraints. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Thermal CVD
nodes.detail: Heat drives reactions at the wafer.

nodes.label: Plasma-enhanced CVD
nodes.detail: Activated species enable useful reactions at lower temperatures.

nodes.label: Process-specific variants
nodes.detail: Film density, conformality and gap filling guide the choice.

title: Separate two self-limiting surface reactions
caption: Purges keep precursor pulses apart; each half-reaction saturates available surface sites before the next begins. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Precursor A pulse
nodes.detail: The first reactant binds to available surface sites.

nodes.label: Purge A
nodes.detail: Remove excess precursor and gaseous by-products.

nodes.label: Reactant B pulse
nodes.detail: The second reactant converts the adsorbed layer.

nodes.label: Purge B
nodes.detail: Clear the chamber before repeating the cycle.

title: Sputtering is physical transport from target to wafer
caption: Ions eject atoms from a solid target; line-of-sight arrival helps explain why deep recessed coverage is difficult. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Argon ions
nodes.detail: The plasma supplies energetic projectiles.

nodes.label: Solid target
nodes.detail: Impact dislodges atoms from the desired material.

nodes.label: Traveling flux
nodes.detail: Atoms move across the chamber toward exposed surfaces.

nodes.label: Substrate film
nodes.detail: Arrival and sticking create the deposited layer.

title: Epitaxy copies the crystal while changing composition
caption: A compatible substrate supplies lattice order; controlled growth can create doped regions or alternating material layers. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Engineered epitaxial layer
nodes.detail: The deposited crystal inherits the template orientation while growth controls its composition and doping.

nodes.label: Crystalline template
nodes.detail: The substrate supports epitaxial growth.

title: A stressed film bends its substrate
caption: Intrinsic growth effects and thermal mismatch contribute to film stress; curvature is a mechanical response of the stack. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Tensile film stress
nodes.detail: The film tends to contract relative to its constraint.

nodes.label: Compressive film stress
nodes.detail: The film tends to expand relative to its constraint.

nodes.label: Wafer curvature
nodes.detail: The substrate bends in response to the net stress.

title: One film needs several kinds of evidence
caption: Thickness, composition, structure and stress are distinct properties; complementary measurements constrain the process. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Optical measurements
nodes.detail: Reflected polarization or spectra help infer thickness and optical properties.

nodes.label: Structural measurements
nodes.detail: Diffraction and related methods probe order or composition.

nodes.label: Curvature measurements
nodes.detail: Bending provides evidence of film stress.

nodes.label: Qualified film
nodes.detail: The combined properties determine suitability for the device.

title: Deposition tools specialize around different film jobs
caption: The equipment market comprises several process families; capability and qualification matter alongside overall spending. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Thermal batch films
nodes.detail: Furnaces support selected high-temperature materials.

nodes.label: Conformal growth
nodes.detail: ALD and related processes serve complex geometries.

nodes.label: Metal deposition
nodes.detail: PVD and other routes build conductive layers.

nodes.label: Integrated device flow
nodes.detail: Multiple tool families cooperate across one chip process.
